subject: RFI: TAM shift handoffs, on-call coverage, and incident notification playbook
messages:
From: Olivia Matthews <olivia.matthews@firstshore.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: FirstShore Procurement <procurement@firstshore.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: TAM shift handoffs, on-call coverage, and incident notification playbook

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this — attached is our vendor RFI template specific to support and TAM operations. We need detailed answers for: shift handover process between TAMs, guaranteed on-call coverage windows (including regional fallbacks), incident notification timing and channels for P1/P2 events, and a sample notification playbook we can review.

Can you return the completed spreadsheet and any supporting docs by EOD Tuesday (we're trying to finalize vendor short-listing this week)? If you have standard templates (playbooks, roster/export of on-call shifts) that would speed our review.

Appreciate it — Olivia

Attachments: FirstShore_RFI_Template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Matthews <olivia.matthews@firstshore.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: TAM shift handoffs, on-call coverage, and incident notification playbook

Hi Olivia — thanks for sending this over. We've started populating the template; a couple quick clarifying questions to make sure we align with your expectations:

1) When you say "guaranteed on-call coverage windows", do you require 24x7 primary TAM coverage for escalation triage, or is a defined 9am-9pm support window acceptable with an after-hours emergency route?

2) For regional fallbacks, do you prefer routing by geography or by SLA tier (e.g., production-critical vs. non-critical)?

3) For the notification playbook, do you want a single consolidated PDF or per-environment (prod/stage) variants?

If it's helpful, we can share a draft playbook and our current TAM shift roster as a single package — I can send that to you by EOD today.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-29T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: RFI: TAM shift handoffs, on-call coverage, and incident notification playbook

Team — forwarding FirstShore's RFI (attached). They need: shift handoffs, on-call coverage window, incident notification timings and channels, and a sample playbook. Deadline: EOD Tue (they're fast-tracking).

Draft plan: I'll fill the RFI with high-level answers (we default to 9am-9pm primary, 24x7 emergency after-hours routing to on-call SRE/TAM pool) but need your operational confirmation and any edits. Specific asks:
- Laura: can you export the current TAM roster and a sample week of shifts (UTC offset included)? Prefer PDF export with names obfuscated if necessary.
- Vivek: please confirm escalation times for P1 (error surge/system-down) and P2 (degraded performance) and the exact channels (PagerDuty, email, SMS). Also include our escalation SLA targets (time-to-ack and time-to-incident-owner).
- Camila: review the sample playbook language for wording around customer-facing notifications and any legal phrasing we should avoid.

I'll merge everything into the spreadsheet and produce a single playbook file. If you can get your items to me by 3pm PT today I can send the consolidated response to FirstShore this evening.

Thanks — Karthik

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-29T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: TAM shift handoffs, on-call coverage, and incident notification playbook

Karthik / Vivek —

Attached are two files: 1) redwood_tam_shifts_and_roster.pdf — anonymized week export (UTC offsets included), and 2) incident_notification_playbook_v1.docx — our standard customer-facing playbook (internal reviewed). Highlights:

- Handoffs: we use a 15-minute overlap for shift-to-shift handoffs and a documented handoff checklist (ongoing tickets, open incidents, outstanding customer items). Handoff checklist is section 2 of the playbook.
- Coverage windows: primary TAM coverage 09:00–21:00 local business hours (customer's primary timezone) with a 24x7 emergency on-call pool (SRE + senior TAM rotation) for P1 events. We propose regional fallback (US/EU/APAC) to minimize latency and respect labor/take-home laws.
- Escalation timings (Vivek — confirm SLA numbers below): target ack for P1 = 15 minutes, incident owner assigned within 30 minutes; P2 ack = 60 minutes, owner assigned within 4 hours.

If Vivek confirms SLA numbers I can finalize the playbook copy. Camila — flagged a few customer-facing lines where we should avoid 'guarantee' language; see comments in the DOCX.

Attachments: redwood_tam_shifts_and_roster.pdf (PDF), incident_notification_playbook_v1.docx (docx)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Matthews <olivia.matthews@firstshore.com>
Cc: FirstShore Procurement <procurement@firstshore.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: TAM shift handoffs, on-call coverage, and incident notification playbook — submitted

Hi Olivia — attached is our completed RFI template plus two supporting artifacts: redwood_tam_shifts_and_roster.pdf and incident_notification_playbook_v1.docx. Below is a short summary of the responses:

- Coverage model: Primary TAM coverage during customer-local business hours (09:00–21:00 local) with a dedicated 24x7 emergency on-call pool for P1 incidents. We recommend regional fallback routing (US/EU/APAC) to ensure response overlap and comply with local requirements.
- Handoffs: 15-minute overlap between shifts; standardized handoff checklist captured in the playbook (section 2).
- Escalation SLAs: P1: ack within 15 minutes, incident owner within 30 minutes. P2: ack within 60 minutes, owner within 4 hours.
- Notification channels: PagerDuty for immediate paging (P1), SMS escalation for critical ownership, automated status emails to subscribed stakeholders, and a Postmortem/Incident doc link within 48 hours for major incidents.

Attachments included: FirstShore_RFI_Template.xlsx (completed), redwood_tam_shifts_and_roster.pdf, incident_notification_playbook_v1.docx.

Next steps: happy to hop on a 30-minute walkthrough with your procurement and ops team to talk through the playbook and local onboarding. Does Thursday 10am ET or Friday 2pm ET work?

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193
